body: Stood in front of the sunburst mesa this morning — the repository as terraces, the big vendored files sitting there like mesas of their own. It reads beautifully. You can tell where the weight of the project lives without a single number being printed.
One request: when I descend into demo-de, keep the path from the root in view. Losing the way back is the one thing a good map never does to you.
messages.snippet: Stood in front of the sunburst mesa this morning — the repository as terraces…
messages.subject: The mesa reads beautifully

body: A sheet of paper per job is exactly right. The half-fed sheet for the job being printed made me laugh — it is the whole state of the machine in one gesture, no progress bar required.
If the queue ever grows past a dozen, let the sheets fan rather than stack. A fan reads as abundance; a tall stack reads as a problem.
messages.snippet: A sheet of paper per job is exactly right. The half-fed sheet for the job…
messages.subject: The press queue, as geometry

body: You said the master view is a snow globe — a miniature world under glass, everything contained and turning slowly. Then the web frame should bring one home: capture a page about snow globes and stand it on the dais, structure and all.
Detach, not screenshot. A picture of a page is a souvenir; its headings and links, laid out as furniture, are the thing itself, visiting.
messages.snippet: You said the master view is a snow globe — a miniature world under glass…
messages.subject: A snow globe for the shelf

body: The tangled tree's second course wants an atlas: one sheet per level of the import graph, the entry modules along the top, the deep utilities at the bottom where the rivers end.
A module's progeny being its dependency closure is the right measure. It is what a maintainer actually fears when they touch a file.
messages.snippet: The tangled tree's second course wants an atlas: one sheet per level…
messages.subject: Atlas sheets for the import graph

body: Title page alone on the first recto — yes. A book that opens wrong teaches you to distrust every page after it, and this one opens like a book should.
The drum turning the accessed chapter to the front is the cylinder's answer to a thumb index. Keep the ghosting gentle; a reader should sense the rest of the book, not lose it.
messages.snippet: Title page alone on the first recto — yes. A book that opens wrong…
messages.subject: Binding the cylinder book

body: Chapters, sections, pages; folders, subfolders, letters. The space keeps choosing tiers, and the back keys keep climbing them one level at a time. That consistency is the whole interaction language — guard it.
When mail arrives as a citizen, let its folders be tiers in the same sense. A folder you can stand in front of, a letter you can take out.
messages.snippet: Chapters, sections, pages; folders, subfolders, letters. The space keeps…
messages.subject: Tiers all the way down

body: The distinction matters: the dolly moves the camera, the window zoom moves the frame across the samples. In the waveform app you feel it immediately — the fence stays stood on the stage while the window slides over the track.
Honest buckets, too. A zoom that invents detail is a liar with good rendering.
messages.snippet: The distinction matters: the dolly moves the camera, the window zoom…
messages.subject: Zoom inside the frame

body: Eleven entry modules at level zero. The relaxation that levels them is cycle-safe by construction, which is fortunate, because real import graphs are never as acyclic as we promise they are.
Switching courses clearing the hover is correct behaviour, by the way. A figure in one course is not an address in the other.
messages.snippet: Eleven entry modules at level zero. The relaxation that levels them…
messages.subject: The import graph, second course

body: PLAN, ELEVATION, SIDE, HOME — the digits call the same goView as the fieldset buttons and the command line, so there is exactly one door to each view and three handles on it.
A named view also levels the platter's camera-space turns. An absolute seat cannot argue with a leftover rotation.
messages.snippet: PLAN, ELEVATION, SIDE, HOME — the digits call the same goView…
messages.subject: Views, in the fieldset's order

body: The converter strategy in three words. Carry a page as it is, on a frame. Detach its structure into the space's own furniture — headings, sections, links as things you can address. Then, for the places that matter, build native citizens.
The captured page is the detach proof. The live version waits on a local bridge driving a real browser, and that is a later slice, honestly labelled.
messages.snippet: The converter strategy in three words. Carry a page as it is…
messages.subject: Carry, detach, native

body: Magnify grows the thing; the dolly moves you. Confusing them is how a space ends up with a giant object and a lost traveller. The opened citizen taking the dolly — travelling into the thing you opened — is the correct instinct.
Filed under archive because the argument is settled, not because it is old.
messages.snippet: Magnify grows the thing; the dolly moves you. Confusing them is how…
messages.subject: On dollies and other travellers

body: Do not confine the thing to its semisphere. Let the base yield: the protective sphere is a fact of rotation, and the floor subtracts itself where the sphere would pass. A tall object carries a larger sphere and carves a wider well — that is the rule working, not failing.
The floor holding level while the world tips over it is the tell. A base that tips with the world was never a base.
messages.snippet: Do not confine the thing to its semisphere. Let the base yield…
messages.subject: The well under the platter
